set: Quillbrook Village Hall
role: governing
covers: "Trustee membership, voting, meetings and decision-making authority"
---
# Trustee Committee Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Purpose
1.1 The committee manages the hall for community use.
1.2 It may hire out rooms and equipment under hall-bookings.md.
1.3 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.

## 2. Committee membership
2.1 The committee has between five and nine trustees.
2.2 Trustees must be at least 18 years old.
2.3 Applicants must live in Quillbrook or a neighbouring village.
2.4 A trustee serves for two years and may stand again.
2.5 Trustees receive no payment for committee work.

## 3. Appointment and departure
3.1 New trustees are elected at the annual public meeting.
3.2 Election requires more than half of votes cast.
3.3 The committee may fill vacancies until the next annual meeting.
3.4 A trustee may resign by giving written notice.
3.5 Three consecutive missed meetings without explanation trigger a review.

## 4. Meetings and votes
4.1 The committee meets at least six times each calendar year.
4.2 Four trustees form a quorum.
4.3 Decisions require a majority of those present and voting.
4.4 The chair has a casting vote if votes are equal.
4.5 Minutes must be approved at the next meeting.

## 5. Spending authority
5.1 The treasurer may approve routine spending up to £150.
5.2 Spending above £150 requires a committee vote.
5.3 Emergency safety spending follows hall-safety.md section 5.
5.4 Two trustees must approve payments above £500.

## 6. Matters not covered
6.1 These rules do not set a maximum number of trustee terms.
6.2 They do not prescribe a method for resolving personal disputes.
6.3 They do not specify whether trustees may attend remotely.

content.text:
**The rules don't say whether a remote trustee counts towards quorum, so I can't give a definite yes or no. Whether the meeting is quorate depends on a question the rules leave open.**

- **Quorum:** Rule 4.2 says "Four trustees form a quorum." The rules don't say those four must be physically present.
- **Remote attendance:** Rule 6.3 says the rules "do not specify whether trustees may attend remotely." Nothing else in the hall documents mentions remote or video attendance either.
- **Your meeting:** Three trustees in the room plus one on video makes four attending. The meeting is quorate only if the video attendee counts as one of the four.

**If the remote trustee counts:** the meeting is quorate with exactly four. Any one of the four dropping out, for example through a connection failure, would make it inquorate. Decisions need a majority of those present and voting (4.3), and the chair has a casting vote on a tie (4.4).

**If the remote trustee doesn't count:** only three are present, so the meeting is inquorate and can't make valid decisions.

Because the rules are silent, the safer course is one of these:
1. Have the committee agree, ideally minuted at an earlier meeting, that remote attendees count towards quorum.
2. Get a fourth trustee to attend in person on 15 November 2026. The rules give the committee five to nine trustees (2.1), so at least one more should be available.
3. Check whether the hall has any other governing document, such as a constitution, that covers remote attendance. I found nothing in the files here.

If the meeting goes ahead on the video-call basis alone, any decisions could be challenged as made without a quorum.
